newsitem.title: UK: BG won't comment on German divestment report.
newsitem.headline: BG won't comment on German divestment report.

text.p: Britain's BG Plc, formerly known as British Gas Plc, on Wednesday declined to comment on a report that it has put its German downstream assets up for sale.

The European Gas Markets magazine reported BG plans to divest its five percent stake in Leipzig-based Verbundnetz Gas (VNG) as well as its 25.5 percent and 24 percent holdings in respectively Erdgas West-Sachsen (EWS) and Gasversorgung Sachsen-Anhalt (GSA).
These interests were acquired in 1991, following the collapse of communism and the re-unification of Germany.

VNG is a gas transmission company serving the eastern part of the country. EWS and GSA are more regional, operating respectively in Leipzig and the Halle region with each having around 90,000 customers.
The European Gas Markets magazine said that big German power companies were seen as potential buyers of BG's holdings.
The twice-monthly magazine also cited Statoil as a candidate buyer.
